CLASS zcl_aai_gui_tools IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD get_screenshot.

    DATA: l_mime_type      TYPE string,
          l_file_extension TYPE string,
          l_image          TYPE xstring.

    cl_gui_frontend_services=>get_screenshot(
      IMPORTING
        mime_type_str        = l_mime_type
        image                = l_image
      EXCEPTIONS
        access_denied        = 1
        cntl_error           = 2
        error_no_gui         = 3
        not_supported_by_gui = 4
        OTHERS               = 5
    ).

    IF sy-subrc <> 0.

      IF sy-subrc = 1.
        r_response = 'Error: access denied.'.
      ELSE.
        r_response = 'An error occurred while generating screenshot.'.
      ENDIF.

    ELSE.

      r_response = 'Here is the requested screenshot.'.

      SPLIT l_mime_type AT '/' INTO DATA(l_dummy) l_file_extension.

      IF l_file_extension IS NOT INITIAL.
        l_file_extension = condense( '.' && l_file_extension ).
      ENDIF.

      e_t_files = VALUE #( ( content = cl_http_utility=>encode_x_base64( unencoded = l_image )
                             filename = |screenshot{ l_file_extension }|
                             file_size = xstrlen( l_image )
                             file_type = l_mime_type ) ).

    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD get_clipboard_data.

    DATA lt_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_row.

    cl_gui_frontend_services=>clipboard_import(
      IMPORTING
        data                 = lt_data
        length               = DATA(l_length)
      EXCEPTIONS
        cntl_error           = 1                " Control error
        error_no_gui         = 2                " No GUI available
        not_supported_by_gui = 3                " GUI does not support this
        OTHERS               = 4
    ).

    IF sy-subrc <> 0.

      r_response = 'Error while importing data from the clipboard.'.

    ELSE.

      IF lt_data IS INITIAL.
        r_response = 'The clipboard is empty.'.
      ENDIF.

      LOOP AT lt_data ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<l_row>).

        IF r_response IS INITIAL.
          r_response = <l_row>.
        ELSE.
          r_response = |{ r_response }{ cl_abap_char_utilities=>newline }{ <l_row> }|.
        ENDIF.

      ENDLOOP.

    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD set_clipboard_data.

    DATA lt_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_row.

    DATA l_rc TYPE i.

    SPLIT i_clipboard_data AT cl_abap_char_utilities=>newline INTO TABLE lt_data.

    cl_gui_frontend_services=>clipboard_export(
      IMPORTING
        data                 = lt_data                 " Data
      CHANGING
        rc                   = l_rc                 " Return Code
      EXCEPTIONS
        cntl_error           = 1                " Control error
        error_no_gui         = 2                " No GUI available
        not_supported_by_gui = 3                " GUI does not support this
        no_authority         = 4                " Authorization check failed
        OTHERS               = 5
    ).

    IF sy-subrc <> 0 OR l_rc <> 0.

      r_response = 'Error while exporting data to the clipboard.'.

    ELSE.

      LOOP AT lt_data ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<l_row>).

        IF r_response IS INITIAL.
          r_response = <l_row>.
        ELSE.
          r_response = |{ r_response }{ cl_abap_char_utilities=>newline }{ <l_row> }|.
        ENDIF.

      ENDLOOP.

    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

In case you want to test these tools, edit the function module Z_F_EVENT_FCODE_YAAI and update its code by adding them in the lo_function_calling->add_methods method call, similarly to what we did when we added the Personal Address tools.

Other examples of tools you can build:

  • Call a transaction, similar to a drill-down report.
  • Perform background tasks.
  • Read, write, upload, and download files.
  • Send emails.
  • ... and certainly many, many more! 🙂

A System-Wide Entry Point: Adding the AI Assistant to MENUSYST

As discussed in the General Technical Prerequisites section, adding an entry point for the AI Assistant usually means finding a suitable enhancement for each transaction. There is another option: adding an item to the SAP standard system menu, MENUSYST, to provide a common way to launch the Assistant across transactions, without enhancing each transaction’s user interface individually.

I'm generally opposed to modifying SAP standard objects. I would consider it only in very exceptional cases and only when the change poses no risk to the system’s existing functionality. This approach does involve a standard-system change, which may require minor adjustments during upgrades.

The required changes are:

Transaction: SE41

Program: MENUSYST

Status: MEN

 

 

Transaction: SE37

Function Module: HELP_START

 

With this approach, we can provide a system-wide entry point that determines whether the AI Assistant can be launched in the current transaction and, if so, which assistant to instantiate, along with the appropriate system instructions and tools.

 

 

Closing Thoughts

That's it for this post! I hope the ideas and examples shared here give you a good starting point for integrating AI assistants into your SAP system.

There are many ways to approach this, and the right solution will depend on the transactions you want to enhance and the extension options available in your SAP environment.

I'd love to hear about your experiences, what you build, and what you learn along the way.

entry.title: SAP TechEd 2026 Berlin: Key Innovations, AI Breakthroughs and What's New in the SAP Ecosystem
entry.content:
SAP TechEd 2026 brings a new wave of enterprise innovation, putting AI agents, Joule Work, intelligent automation and connected business data at the center of the Autonomous Enterprise vision.

SAP TechEd 2026, held in Berlin, highlights SAP's continued commitment to transforming how businesses operate through artificial intelligence, intelligent automation and next-generation enterprise solutions.

This year's announcements reflect a major shift in SAP's AI strategy: moving beyond AI-powered assistance toward autonomous enterprise operations, where AI agents can understand business objectives, coordinate workflows, interact with enterprise applications and execute complex tasks with appropriate governance.

From enhancements to Joule Work and Joule Studio to the introduction of SAP Business AI Platform capabilities, SAP Business Data Cloud innovations and new AI models, TechEd 2026 introduces several developments that will shape the future of enterprise technology.

Let's explore the key announcements and innovations from SAP TechEd 2026.

1. Joule Work: Moving Towards Autonomous Business Operations

One of the biggest highlights of SAP TechEd 2026 is the continued evolution of Joule Work, SAP's AI-powered user experience designed to simplify complex business operations.

Joule Work enables users to describe a business goal in natural language, while AI orchestrates the required agents, applications and data across SAP and non-SAP systems to accomplish the task.

Some of the key enhancements include:

  • Advanced agentic thinking: Improved reasoning, planning and execution capabilities for complex business workflows.
  • Enterprise governance: Built-in audit trails, role-based permissions and human-in-the-loop checkpoints.
  • Expanded SAP Knowledge Graph integration: Better business context to help AI agents understand customer-specific processes and data.
  • Secure agent-to-agent interoperability: Improved connectivity between SAP Joule Agents and third-party AI agents through a secure gateway.

These developments represent an important step toward an enterprise environment where AI agents can collaborate and execute connected business processes securely.

2. Joule Studio: Simplifying Enterprise AI Agent Development

SAP is also expanding Joule Studio, making it easier for developers and business users to build, customize and manage AI agents.

With deeper integration into Joule Work, Joule Studio provides a shared environment for creating custom agents, extending existing Joule Agents and orchestrating workflows.

Key innovations include:

  • Intent-based development: Developers can describe business requirements, and Joule Studio helps identify relevant processes, APIs, data and authorizations.
  • AI agent extensions: Existing Joule Agents can be enhanced with additional instructions, APIs, MCP connections and workflow triggers.
  • n8n integration: Enables orchestration of complex workflows across SAP and non-SAP applications.
  • Agent lifecycle management: New capabilities for testing, evaluating, deploying and monitoring agents.
  • Developer flexibility: Business users can define requirements through the web experience, while developers can continue working through their preferred IDE and CLI tools.

SAP is also introducing pre-deployment testing and offline evaluations to help organizations validate agent behavior before production deployment.

The objective is to make enterprise AI development more accessible while maintaining the governance and security required for business-critical applications.

3. SAP Business AI Platform: Building the Foundation for Enterprise AI

The SAP Business AI Platform is a major part of SAP's Autonomous Enterprise strategy.

It brings together the capabilities required to build, contextualize, reason and govern enterprise AI solutions.

The platform focuses on combining business process knowledge, trusted enterprise data, AI models and governance capabilities to help organizations move beyond isolated AI pilots.

Key announcements include:

SAP Enterprise AI Gateway

A new centralized governance solution designed to manage AI interactions across enterprise environments.

It will provide:

  • Centralized authentication and authorization.
  • AI traffic routing and policy enforcement.
  • Monitoring and usage tracking.
  • Auditing and governance.
  • Secure connectivity across MCPs, APIs, AI agents and large language models.

Built on SAP Integration Suite, the solution aims to simplify the management of enterprise AI interactions.

General availability is planned for Q1 2027.

SAP AI Agent Hub

SAP is expanding AI agent governance capabilities to provide better visibility and control over SAP and third-party AI agents.

A new AI Governance Assistant will also help organizations assess AI systems against regulatory requirements, including the EU AI Act.

This will support risk classification, documentation reviews and ongoing compliance assessments.

4. SAP Business Data Cloud: Advancing Enterprise Data Management

Data remains one of the most important foundations for successful enterprise AI adoption.

At TechEd 2026, SAP announced new SAP Business Data Cloud capabilities designed to make enterprise data more accessible, reusable and valuable for AI and analytics.

Some major innovations include:

Expanded Lakehouse Capabilities

SAP is introducing native support for Apache Iceberg and a distributed SQL query engine, supported by Dremio technology.

These capabilities will help organizations access and process SAP and third-party data across hybrid and multi-cloud environments.

Potential benefits include:

  • Reduced data duplication.
  • Faster access to business insights.
  • Improved query performance.
  • Greater flexibility in data architecture.
  • Consistent governance across data environments.

SAP Business Data Cloud Ontology Manager

A new AI-assisted solution designed to help organizations create and manage domain-specific business ontologies.

It will enable businesses to organize relationships, rules and processes into reusable business context that AI agents can understand.

Enhanced SAP Knowledge Graph

SAP Knowledge Graph will gain support for additional SAP-managed and customer-managed data products.

This will help Joule and other AI agents understand company-specific business relationships and provide more relevant, context-aware responses.

Together, these innovations strengthen SAP's business data fabric strategy and provide a more reliable foundation for enterprise AI.

5. SAP HANA Cloud: AI-Powered Database Administration

SAP is bringing new agentic AI capabilities to SAP HANA Cloud to simplify database administration.

Database administrators will be able to use a conversational interface to perform tasks such as:

  • Monitoring database health.
  • Troubleshooting technical issues.
  • Optimizing SQL queries and database performance.
  • Managing database lifecycle operations.
  • Diagnosing and resolving operational issues.

These capabilities aim to reduce repetitive administrative work and allow database teams to focus on strategic activities.

General availability is planned for Q4 2026.

6. SAP-RPT AI Models: Smarter Predictions and Business Decisions

SAP is expanding its SAP-RPT family of AI models to improve the way AI understands and works with structured enterprise data.

Unlike traditional large language models, which primarily focus on unstructured information, tabular AI is designed to understand structured business data and support more accurate predictions.

Three important developments were announced:

  • SAP-RPT-TS: A time-series forecasting model designed for business scenarios such as demand forecasting. Generally available.
  • SAP-RPT-Decisions: A decision intelligence model designed to automate business decisions across workflows. General availability planned for Q4 2026.
  • SAP-RPT-2: An expanded model supporting multi-table processing, anomaly detection and structured data embeddings. General availability planned for Q1 2027.

SAP also announced the deployment of SAP-RPT on HPE Spaceborne Computer-2 aboard the International Space Station, demonstrating the potential of enterprise AI in edge-computing environments.

7. SAP Document AI: Advancing Intelligent Document Processing

SAP is introducing new capabilities in SAP Document AI to make document processing more intelligent and autonomous.

The new SAP-DOC-1 AI model is designed to extract information from different document formats without extensive upfront configuration.

Additional enhancements include:

  • Document splitting for processing complex, multi-page documents.
  • Custom prompting to define specific information extraction requirements.
  • Deeper integration with Joule Work.
  • Joule Studio capabilities for building document-aware agents and workflows.

These developments will help businesses automate document-intensive processes and reduce manual intervention.

General availability is planned for Q1 2027.

8. SAP Integration Suite: Stronger Connectivity and AI-Driven Integration

As enterprises adopt more AI agents, seamless connectivity between applications and systems becomes increasingly important.

SAP Integration Suite is receiving several enhancements to support modern integration requirements.

Key announcements include:

  • AI-assisted message processing error resolution.
  • AI-based detection of unusual API request payload sizes.
  • Enhanced GitHub integration for managing integration artifacts.
  • Native RosettaNet support for B2B and supply chain integration.
  • New third-party application adapters for Gmail, Google Sheets, GoToWebinar, Microsoft Excel and Salesforce Service Cloud.
  • Improved monitoring through SAP Cloud ALM.

These enhancements will help organizations simplify integration development, improve operational visibility and prepare their enterprise landscapes for agentic AI.

9. SAP Cloud ERP and RISE with SAP: AI-Driven Transformation

SAP is also evolving the RISE with SAP methodology to help customers adopt AI more effectively as part of their business transformation journeys.

The upcoming enhancements include:

  • AI-enriched implementation guidance and best practices.
  • Personalized onboarding across SAP Autonomous Suite.
  • AI readiness assessments that connect business priorities with relevant AI use cases.
  • Structured transformation road maps to help organizations measure business value.

The focus is on helping customers move beyond technology implementation and achieve measurable business outcomes through AI adoption.

General availability is planned for Q1 2027.

10. New SAP Certifications and Learning Opportunities

Alongside its technology announcements, SAP is investing in building the skills required for the next generation of enterprise AI professionals.

Two important learning developments include:

SAP Business AI Platform Solution Architect Certification

A new certification designed for developers, consultants, partners and solution architects.

It validates expertise across three major platform pillars:

  • Build.
  • Contextualize and reason.
  • Govern.

Joule Studio Developer Certification

SAP has also introduced a Joule Studio developer certification focused on building, extending and managing enterprise AI agents.

As part of its introductory offer, the certification is available free of charge through December 31, 2026.

These learning opportunities provide SAP professionals with a chance to strengthen their expertise in enterprise AI and agentic development.

What Does SAP TechEd 2026 Mean for the Future of Enterprise Technology?

The announcements at SAP TechEd 2026 highlight a significant evolution in the enterprise software landscape.

SAP is moving toward an ecosystem where AI is not simply an assistant that answers questions but an intelligent capability that understands business context, collaborates with other agents and helps execute business processes.

A few major trends stand out:

  1. From generative AI to agentic AI: AI agents are becoming more capable of planning and executing complex workflows.
  2. From disconnected systems to connected intelligence: SAP is strengthening interoperability across SAP and third-party applications.
  3. From generic AI to business-aware AI: SAP Knowledge Graph and Business Data Cloud provide the context needed for enterprise-specific intelligence.
  4. From AI experimentation to enterprise governance: Security, compliance, monitoring and controlled execution are becoming essential components of AI adoption.
  5. From manual development to intent-based development: Tools such as Joule Studio are making it easier to translate business requirements into AI-powered solutions.

Final Thoughts

SAP TechEd 2026 reinforces SAP's vision of the Autonomous Enterprise, where people, business applications, trusted data and intelligent AI agents work together to simplify operations and accelerate business outcomes.

With innovations across Joule Work, Joule Studio, SAP Business AI Platform, SAP Business Data Cloud, SAP HANA Cloud and SAP Integration Suite, SAP is building the foundation for the next generation of intelligent enterprise solutions.

For SAP customers, developers, consultants and technology professionals, these announcements create exciting opportunities to explore agentic AI, modern enterprise architecture and intelligent automation.

The future of SAP is moving beyond simply running business processes. It is about making those processes more intelligent, connected and autonomous.

For the complete list of announcements, product updates, availability timelines and technical details, visit SAP's official announcement guide:

SAP TechEd 2026 Innovation News Guide
